text: Testing data pipelines — filling in what lesson 45's test stage actually runs.

Unit tests check one transformation in isolation. Schema tests catch drift before it reaches production. Row-count tests catch a run that silently processed zero rows, or ten times too many. Regression tests catch a query that quietly changed shape.
Neither of these examples is complicated — checking a fare is never negative, checking a row count falls in a plausible range. Both catch a real mistake, automatically, every single run.

A data pipeline test has to also ask whether its input is even representative of real production data — hand-picked rows can pass while missing a real problem entirely. Next up: unit testing PySpark transformations, in full depth.
